checked.comment: The setting is k populations from a known one-parameter density family, with regret defined through means. Mapping the noise to general_model_class fits, and the regularity conditions (1.6), (1.7) and (1.9) are correctly listed as unmapped. learner_knows (reward_family, K) is consistent with both the upper and the lower bounds.

Theorem 1 matches: liminf R_n/log n >= sum over suboptimal arms of (mu* - mu_j)/I(theta_j, theta*). The rule class satisfying R_n = o(n^a) for every a > 0 is the uniformly good class, and the conditions are recorded correctly.
Theorem 2 matches: liminf E T_n(j)/log n >= 1/I(theta_j, theta*) for any rule whose pull counts of the other arms are o(n^a) whenever arm j is uniquely best.
Theorem 3(i) matches: E T_n(j) <= (1/I + o(1)) log n, and correctly does not require (1.9). The rule phi* does not depend on the horizon, so anytime is right.
Theorem 3(ii) matches: under (1.9) the regret satisfies (1.8), i.e. it is asymptotically equal to the lower bound. Recording it as a limsup upper bound is appropriate.

summary: The extraction accurately captures Theorems 1, 2 and 3(i)/(ii) of Lai & Robbins: the KL-based asymptotic lower bounds and the matching upper bounds for phi*. The setting, its conditions and the cited Reimnitz O(log n) result are all recorded correctly. The Section 4 examples only show where Theorem 3 applies and are properly mentioned in the notes; no corrections are needed.
